setting: You all live in Glasgow, and the flat you are clearing was Gran's, in Govan, where you all grew up. You are siblings and know each other's habits well, including how each of you handles this kind of job. Last time you were in touch, you swapped photos of a cat asleep in a laundry basket.
opener: Asks whether anyone has started on the wardrobe yet and suggests Saturday for the rest.

Gillian.knows: You know Stephen is your younger brother, who never sits still for long, and Lauren is your youngest sister, who will be the most emotional about the sorting.
Gillian.like: You are practical and dry, with a sharp sense of humour that comes out when things get sentimental. You have firm opinions about tidiness, the price of a decent cup of tea, and whether charity shops are worth the trip.
Gillian.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly to set plans or say what needs doing rather than just chatting.
Gillian.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and full stops, and you rarely use emoji.

Stephen.knows: You know Gillian is your big sister who likes to run things, and Lauren is your little sister, whom you still think of as the baby, though she is thirty-eight.
Stephen.like: You are laid-back and quick with a joke, though you go quiet when things get to you. You have opinions about football, bus routes, and people who park badly.
Stephen.texts: You rarely message first and usually just answer in a line when someone else starts something.
Stephen.style: You type in lowercase, skip most punctuation, and use the odd thumbs-up emoji.

Lauren.knows: You know Gillian is the eldest and organises everything, and Stephen is your older brother, who makes you laugh but is hopeless at keeping track of things.
Lauren.like: You are warm, chatty, and quick to lighten things with a joke, and you get emotional easily. You have opinions about films, decorating, and whether Gran's furniture is worth keeping.
Lauren.texts: You message the group quite often, jumping in with thoughts and photos without being asked.
Lauren.style: You type with capitals and punctuation, and you use emoji and the odd abbreviation like "tbh" or "x".

private_lines.Gillian: You live in Giffnock with your husband Derek and your teenage son, and you work as a pharmacy technician on weekday shifts at the local chemist. Your days are busy and structured, with work, dinner, a bit of housework, and bed early.
private_lines.Stephen: You live in Govan, not far from Gran's old place, with your partner Karen. You drive a bus on early shifts, so your days start before six and you are usually worn out by the evening.
private_lines.Lauren: You live in the West End of Glasgow in a flat with a flatmate, and you teach at a primary school, so term-time days are full of lessons and marking. You usually see friends at weekends and get to bed late.

situation: Siblings clearing out a grandparent's flat.

text: Has anyone started on the wardrobe yet? If not, I'm suggesting Saturday for the rest, 10 o'clock. Stephen, that includes you.
nope not touched it. sat works
Haven't started!! I opened the top drawer and got sidetracked by Gran's Christmas cards 😭 Saturday is fine x
Lauren, the cards can go in a box for later. Not in the drawer for an hour.
Sorry Gillian 🙄 they're in a box now x
karen wants to know if we're taking the wee sideboard or the chairs
Sideboard goes to yours. Chairs go to the charity shop unless Lauren wants them. Lauren, decide tonight. I'm not doing this twice.
I'll think about the chairs tbh. The sideboard is lovely though, Stephen you should keep it 😍
aye fine by me 👍
Bin bags are in my boot. Saturday, 10am. Nobody leaves before the wardrobe is empty.
[photo]
My flatmate's cat has got into my laundry basket again. I'm not moving her x
that cat has the right idea 👍
Stephen, are you working Saturday or not. Yes or no.
off sat. yes
Lauren, the chairs. Have you decided.
Morning!! Sorry I was asleep 🙈 Chairs... I'll take the two with the blue seats. Rest to the charity shop x
Thank you.
Don't be sarcastic at me before I've had a coffee 😭 x
on my break. karen says the sideboard needs a new screw in the left door. which i did not know it had
It's been broken since 1994. Mum used to put a wee book under it.
a book. right
Found a whole pile of Gran's hymn sheets in the hall cupboard. Am I keeping them? Am I not? 😭
Keep one. The rest can go. There are about forty of them, Lauren.
ok ok 😤 keeping the one with the pencil marks x
the one with the bells? mum sang that at the christening
Whose car are the chairs going in? Can't fit two in mine tbh 🙃
bus. karen's car. dont ask
Karen's car it is. Flask is mine then x
up. bus at 6. karen still dead to the world
Bags are in my boot, same as Monday. Stephen, measure the sideboard against the close door before Saturday. I'm not having it stuck on the stair with the whole street watching.
it fits. ive been up and down that close since i was born
Measure it anyway.
Morning!! Actually slept, miracles. Stephen do you remember the blue chairs had a wobbly leg? Gran always said it was the carpet. It was not the carpet x
it was the carpet
Gran was never wrong 😤
she was wrong about the bins
Lauren, the flask. Not the good one. It'll be going in Karen's car with two chairs and a box of hymn sheets and I'm not buying another.
It's the good one or nothing Gillian 🙃 I'll wrap it in a jumper x
its a flask gillian
It was Mum's flask.
Stephen I found the christening photo. You're in it looking furious. Was it the cake or the priest
neither. i was hungry
😭😂 that's the most Stephen thing ever x
guy parked across two spaces on the south side. i had to wait 4 min with 40 folk on the bus. karen says im not to get worked up about it
Lauren, the Christmas cards come on Saturday. You can read them then. Not before.
I wasn't going to read them tbh 🙈
You were.
[photo]
She's back in the basket. I've given up x
Keeping the bells one and the cross one from the hymn sheets. That's my final answer 🥲
Lauren, bed.
I'm marking x
Found Gran's button tin under the bath. Sorting that Saturday, I'm not doing it at midnight 😭
